correctness.rationale: The positive-speed implicit equation Phi(u,v)=uv(v-u)/(u+v)=t and three sine kicks with zero sum yield the exact identity sum_cyclic Phi = -(x-y)(x-z)(y-z)(xy+xz+yz)/((x+y)(x+z)(y+z)). Independently verified symbolically in SymPy; positivity forces repeated speed and hence a zero sine kick. This restricts initial angles to multiples pi/3. With a=sqrt3|P|/2, the positive quadratic root ratio satisfies q²-(1+t/u²)q-t/u²=0. Its negative-kick plus branch is defined exactly for t/u²>=-(3-2sqrt2), and inverse step after a positive kick selects this branch precisely when entering w²>=a. In the opposite order, negative first requires w²>=(3+2sqrt2)a. Both inclusive endpoints are double quadratic roots. The rotating angle has least period three, and the proof covers all positive speeds and P !=0. Finite source verifier is consistency evidence, not universality.
